messages:
alex: quick postmortem follow-up: seen a correctness blip in staging when a slab was reassigned mid-pop. short window (~120ms) where stale values were returned to tenant A after eviction. repro attached.

priya: how deterministic is the repro?

alex: reasonably consistent when we introduce a small network delay for metadata propagate. repro gist: tenant A gets lease token, slab handed to tenant B, B writes new state, A reads with old token and gets stale response before metadata settles.

sam: that implies our weak-lease tokens are effectively valid until metadata shows up. we either need revocation or cease serving stale during handoff.

dario: proposed mitigations: (1) add a "quiescing" slab state that forces reads to miss while handoff completes; (2) rotate per-slab signing keys on handoff so old tokens fail; (3) add an out-of-band revocation broadcast; (4) require clients to validate post-read epoch.

priya: tradeoffs: (1) low complexity, but increases cold reads; (2) secure, but needs key management and rotation propagation; (3) reliable only if control-plane is rock-solid; (4) tough on clients and backcompat.

alex: immediate plan: implement (1) behind feature flag + telemetry. instrument quiesce_count and quiesce_latency. Also add an opt-in allow_stale flag clients can set to accept eventual consistency for lower latency.

morgan: long-term: (2) + a verification cache for signatures to avoid per-read crypto. verify once per signature TTL.

sam: sketch for epoched sigs and cache:
```
# issue lease:
lease = {slab_id:S, epoch:E, owner:Node}
sig = HMAC(key_for_S, serialize(lease))
return token=(lease,sig)

# on read(token):
if verify_cache.contains(sig) and verify_cache[sig] >= E: serve_from_cache
else:
  if verify_sig(sig, key_for_S): verify_cache[sig]=E; serve_from_cache
  else: cache_miss
```

dario: question: where to store key_for_S? owner node holds it and rotates on takeover. rotation acts as implicit revocation, but we must ensure rotation completes before owner starts serving new data. hence quiesce + rotation combination looks sound.

priya: operational considerations: add alert when quiesce_rate > threshold; correlate with rebalances and autoscaler events. Also add a dashboard to see quiesce hotspots by tenant.

alex: I'll open a small PR to add quiesce flag handling and tests that simulate metadata reorder; we'll gate behind FF and canary.

morgan: add a short-runbook appendix describing how to act on quiesce alerts (e.g., check recent rebalances, rollback FF).

infra-bot: rollout plan: patch runtime with FF, canary on 2 nodes, collect metrics for 24h, then progressive rollout.

sam: :thumbsup: I'll review the RFC draft for epoched sigs once PR is in.

alex: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/9988 (WIP).

priya: thanks. small follow-up: add unit test that simulates client allowing stale and ensure we serve stale only when allow_stale=true and token expired TTL matches.

morgan: good catch. we'll reconvene after canary data.
